title: Twenty-four Calls and One Cold Room
subtitle: 健康与医疗 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 健康与医疗（生活与学习·健康的生活方式与医疗）
meta: 主题语境：健康与医疗（生活与学习·健康的生活方式与医疗）　|　核心词汇：doctor　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 doctor 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1945 my mother ① called a doctor that no neighbour in the lane would have trusted, and she said the calling was the whole of the night. The ② doctor, meaning the physician and not the degree, came twenty-four calls and stayed unpaid in the book; a doctor, she said, is the only thing in a night that is judged by how long he is left unthanked.

Every ③ doctor in that lane had the same cold room at the back of the house, and the ④ doctor at the end, meaning the one who came on Sundays and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A doctor, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to wait; my mother said the waiting is the part that fills twenty-four calls.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the doctor was the whole of the letter, meaning the degree and not the physician. The ⑥ doctor, meaning the degree and not any of that, is the only thing in a letter that everybody writes after a name and nobody reads; doctor, he said, is either somebody you call or the only word that means both a physician and a degree. He said the degree is the part they remember.

By 1953 the ⑦ doctor had become a line in a register, and the register had become an argument about the cold room. The ⑧ doctor of the whole thing, my mother wrote in February, was one lane and twenty-four calls of waiting; doctor, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to wait. She said the waiting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ doctor I remember is the one at the end, who last came in 1966 and is still described as the quietest in the lane. A ⑩ doctor, my grandmother said in 1968, is the only one who improves by being thanked; every doctor, she said, is a degree that has agreed to look like a physician. She said the degree was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 医生；大夫（指出诊的那一位）
B. n. 医生（指那位医师本人，与那个学位相对）
C. 固定搭配：call a doctor 请一位医生
D. n. 医生（指周日出诊的那一位）
E. n. 医生；行医（抽象总称，指一条巷子的求医之事）
F. n. 医生（指登记簿上写到、被列名的那一位）
G. n. 博士学位（指姓名后写着的那个头衔）
H. n. 博士（抽象总称，指人人写于姓名后却无人细究的那个）

items.q: called a doctor that no neighbour in the lane would have trusted
The doctor, meaning the physician and not the degree
the doctor was the whole of the letter
the doctor had become a line in a register
The doctor of the whole thing
A doctor, my grandmother said in 1968

answers.why: call a doctor 意为“请一位医生”，1945 年母亲请了一位巷子里没有一位邻居肯信任的医生。
doctor 意为“医生”，指那位医师本人而不是那个学位，他出诊了二十四次而在账簿上没有报酬。
doctor 意为“医生”，指那条巷子里每一位医生，每一位的屋子后头都是同一间冷屋子。
doctor 意为“医生”，指周日出诊的那一位，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
doctor 意为“博士学位”，指姓名后写着的那个头衔，叔叔说这个学位就是那封信里最关键的东西。
doctor 意为“博士”，指人人写于姓名后却无人细究的那个而不是那位医师本人，是信里人人都写、却无人细究的东西。
doctor 意为“医生”，指登记簿上写到、被列名的那一位，到 1953 年这位医生成了登记簿里的一行。
doctor 意为“医生、行医”，母亲二月写道，整件事的求医是一条巷子和二十四次出诊的等待。
doctor 意为“医生”，我记得的是末尾那一位，1966 年最后一次来，至今仍被说成巷子里最安静的一位。
doctor 为抽象总称，祖母 1968 年说，一位医生是唯一会因为被致谢而变得更好的人。
